articles.title: Matthew Moss Food Club Celebrates 10th Anniversary of The Bread and Butter Thing
articles.excerpt: The Matthew Moss food club, part of The Bread and Butter Thing, marked its 10th anniversary with a community celebration, highlighting its role in supporting local families.
articles.content_html:
Members and volunteers at the Matthew Moss food club celebrated the 10th anniversary of The Bread and Butter Thing on Saturday, September 27. The event brought together the community to acknowledge a decade of service and support for local families in need.

The Matthew Moss food club is one of over 160 hubs across England that provide affordable food options to households. For £8.50, members receive three bags of food, which include fresh fruit and vegetables, chilled items, and cupboard staples. The club not only offers food but also serves as a social hub where members can meet their neighbours and volunteer.

Vic Harper, chief executive of The Bread and Butter Thing, expressed gratitude towards the members and volunteers, stating, "People knowing they can rely on us, week after week, is only possible because of the dedicated members, volunteers and partners who make hubs like Matthew Moss such an important part of their community."

The charity, which began with a single van delivering surplus food to a community centre in Moss Side, Manchester, now supports over 100,000 households through its network of hubs. The anniversary celebration included cake and refreshments, fostering a sense of community among attendees.
